chapter: Harlem, 52nd Street and the first big bands
title: Benny Goodman and the Dickie Wells basement kazoo band
summary: Barnet never saw Goodman sit in at Harlem sessions, and recalls a swinging amplified-kazoo band in a basement club.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: I remember Benny Goodman used to go and listen, but he never sat in.
Well, I never saw Benny there, but --
I don't mean at that particular place, but I mean uptown at sessions, I've heard musicians say that Benny Goodman used to go and listen but he never played.
Now that you mention it, having been one of those that did go around to a lot of those places, I

don't ever recall seeing Benny play anyplace. Of course they had a wonderful band down at Dickie Weish1 place, down there in the basement. It was a rhythm section, a real swinging rhythm section, and Kenny Rosewall, I think his name was, Kenny something. And the front line were three kazoos, which were attached -- those old time radio loud speakers with the horn, you know?
And they had arrangements, and boy, this thing just swung like mad.
